review_candidates.description: Workplace Type: Onsite Newmont produces metals the world needs - safely, responsibly and with care for people, communities and the environment. With a 100+ year history, we continue to shape the future of mining through innovation and strong operational performance. By joining our inclusive, world-class team, you can help shape the future of mining and make a meaningful difference. Ahafo South is Ghana’s largest gold mine and Newmont’s flagship operation in Africa. Commercial production began in 2006, and the site has produced more than 10 million ounces of gold. Located in Ghana’s Ahafo Region, Ahafo South operates both open-pit and underground mines and continues to grow, with new projects planned to extend production well beyond 2050. The mine plays an important role in the region as a major employer and a long-standing partner to its host communities. With a large and diverse workforce, many of whom come from neighbouring communities, Ahafo South has built a strong Always Safe culture supported by continuous learning, development and operational excellence. Joining Ahafo South offers the opportunity to build a rewarding long-term career at the forefront of Ghana’s mining industry while contributing to an operation that creates lasting value for host communities and showcases Newmont’s commitment to responsible mining on a global stage. Your Impact Conduct on-site detailed Engineering following inspections and data collection, analysis of issues/concerns, which then support project engineering activities, ensuring alignment with project objectives, technical excellence, and informed decision-making to support project success. As Part Of Our Team, You Will Coordinate assigned engineering work packages for underground development and infrastructure, including interfaces with ventilation, dewatering and water services, electrical distribution, controls, communications, compressed air and other mine services. Review project drawings, specifications, design criteria and technical deliverables for alignment with approved scope, operating requirements, Newmont standards and applicable regulatory requirements, coordinate comments and closeout through the responsible engineer. Conduct regular underground and surface field inspections to verify safety, quality, progress and conformance with Industry Foundation Classes (IFC) drawings, specifications, permits, work methods and project requirements. Support project quality management by reviewing relevant ITPs, witnessing or verifying inspections and tests, recording deficiencies and non-conformances, and tracking technical corrective actions to closure. Monitor contractor technical performance against approved plans and short-term lookaheads, verify field quantities and reported progress, identify constraints or deviations, and provide evidence-based inputs for progress claims and contractor-performance reviews. Provide timely technical inputs to project controls, including verified progress, forecast requirements, schedule constraints, quantity changes, scope-change impacts, risks and opportunities, support corrective actions without assuming ownership of the project-control systems. Identify and assess engineering and execution risks, participate in hazard, design, constructability and operability reviews, verify assigned mitigation actions, and escalate issues affecting safety, design integrity, critical path or operational readiness. Support construction completion, commissioning readiness and handover through walkdowns, punch-list closeout, engineering clarifications, turnover dossiers, O&M/as-built documentation, operational acceptance and transfer of residual technical risks to Operations. Your Training, Skills & Experience Checklist Formal Qualification (including Professional Registrations): Bachelor’s degree in Mining Engineering or Civil Engineering. Experience Minimum three (3) years of relevant engineering experience, preferably involving underground development, infrastructure, mine services or contractor-delivered projects. Technical Skills Working knowledge of underground development cycles and service requirements, including ventilation, water/dewatering, power, communications, compressed air and mine-service interfaces. Ability to interpret engineering drawings, specifications, calculations, schedules and contractor submissions, and to use relevant design, modeling, document and database systems. Practical knowledge of field inspections, QA/QC, ITPs, RFIs/TQs, change control, redlines/as-builts, risk registers and technical reporting. Ability to assess field problems, develop practical options within delegated authority, and escalate matters requiring specialist or accountable-engineer decisions. Strong written and verbal communication, cross-disciplinary collaboration, accurate record keeping and willingness to stop unsafe work. Problem Solving Ability Complete concrete procedural tasks. Follow procedural steps to complete work. Use practical judgment to overcome problems, or requests assistance. See alternatives based on trial & error. Improve working methods using day-to-day experiences, procedures, observations of pattern of events, and trial and error. Self-awareness Social Process Skills: Understand own behaviors and is aware of the impact on others. Adapt their own behavior where necessary in order to get a productive outcome for the wider team. Team Process Able to be an effective team member by listening, clarifying tasks, receiving and providing feedback. Able to be an effective team leader (where applicable) by establishing and maintaining a positive and productive work environment through listening, dealing with different points of view, giving and receiving feedback. Collaboration Build positive working relationships with a diverse range of people across disciplines. Your Work Environment The position is located at the Ahafo South site for Apensu Underground project. At Newmont, our people are our strength and we’re committed to a safe, inclusive and supportive workplace. If you’re passionate about doing work that matters, join Newmont and help shape the future of mining. Learn more about our purpose and values: About Newmont Hear from our people: Life at Newmont Important: Newmont does not ask candidates to pay money or share sensitive personal data outside our secure application process. If this happens, please report it to our Business Integrity team: it.sec@newmont.com.

review_candidates.description: Chief Investment Officer | Arada Capital | ADGM, Abu Dhabi Arada Capital is establishing a dedicated institutional investment platform from ADGM in Abu Dhabi, focused on property, infrastructure and real assets across the UAE, GCC and wider MENA region. The platform will target long-term investment opportunities linked to regional growth, public-private partnerships, urban development and essential infrastructure. We are seeking a Chief Investment Officer to lead the investment agenda at an important stage in the platform’s development. The role offers the scope to shape strategy, governance, capital deployment and market positioning from the outset, while working within a clear institutional framework and a business with regional ambition. Working closely with the CEO and Board, the CIO will define the investment strategy, establish governance and decision-making frameworks, lead priority transactions, oversee capital deployment and build the investment capability required to support a scalable regional platform. Why this role stands out Meaningful influence over investment strategy, governance and market positioning from the platform’s early stages. The opportunity to build from a clear strategic mandate rather than inherit a legacy investment model. Exposure to long-term regional investment themes, including PPPs, real estate-backed investments, energy transition, utilities, digital infrastructure, social infrastructure, healthcare, education and mixed-use development. Direct engagement with regulators, government entities, sovereign wealth funds, institutional investors, developers and global capital partners. A role that combines investment discipline, capital deployment, portfolio oversight and team build-out. Experience And Qualifications Investment experience across property, real estate investment, infrastructure, real assets, private equity, sovereign wealth, institutional investment management, development finance or a comparable platform. Experience operating in investment committee, fund leadership, partner, managing director or equivalent decision-making environments. Track record leading significant investments and portfolio decisions, ideally with aggregate transaction exposure exceeding USD 1 billion. Strong capability across investment strategy, capital deployment, underwriting, portfolio construction, governance, asset management and value creation. PPP, project finance, concession-based investment or infrastructure fund experience strongly preferred. Bachelor’s degree required; MBA, CFA, CAIA or equivalent advanced qualification preferred. International exposure to mature property and infrastructure markets, particularly the UK or Australia, would be advantageous. Why consider this role? This is an opportunity to help shape a new platform with strategic backing, regional relevance and long-term growth potential. The CIO will help set the investment architecture, attract and deploy capital, build the team and establish Arada Capital’s credibility as a regional investor in property, infrastructure and real assets. The role will suit someone who has built credibility in institutional investment environments and is looking for a mandate with greater strategic influence, visibility and long-term impact.

review_candidates.description: Org. Setting and Reporting The UN Secretary-General launched on 1 January 2019 a bold and new global reform which repositioned the UN Development System to deliver more effectively and efficiently with the achievement of the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). As part of this reform, UN Resident Coordinator Offices (UN RCO), under the leadership of an empowered and independent UN Resident Coordinator - the highest-ranking official of the UN Development System and Representative of the UN Secretary-General at country level - support countries in the achievement of their development priorities and the attainment of the SDGs. In its Resolution A/RES/72/279, the United Nations General Assembly endorsed the transformation of the Development Operations Coordination Office (DCO) as a stand-alone coordination office within the United Nations Secretariat. DCO exercises managerial and oversight functions of the Resident Coordinator System under the oversight of the Chair of United Nations Sustainable Development Group (UNSDG). In 2026, DCO undertook a recalibration to ensure the RC system remains optimally configured to support the acceleration of the 2030 Agenda and embodies the UN 2.0 shift- anchored in data, digital, innovation, behavioral science, strategic foresight, and a mission driven organizational culture. The Associate Data Specialist contributes to interacting with counterparts, officers and technical staff in relevant organizational units in data engineering, data science and other data specialists, data owners and subject matter experts for the development and implementation of the databases, data collection systems and data analytics that optimize statistical efficiency and quality. It also contributes to the interaction with external counterparts in the UN funds, programs and other UN specialized agencies, consultants, and NGOs to collaborate and exchange information and best practices. Specifically, this position is situated in the Office of the United Nations Resident Coordinator in Nairobi, Kenya, and reports to the Development Coordination Officer (Data Management and Results Monitoring/Reporting), under the overall guidance of the Head of the Resident Coordinator's Office. The incumbent will interact closely with colleagues across resident and non-resident UN entities, government counterparts — including the national statistical system — development partners, civil society organizations, academic institutions and other stakeholders involved in the implementation and monitoring of the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF). The incumbent will support the United Nations Country Team (UNCT), Results Groups and the Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Group through the consolidation, validation and quality assurance of agency inputs; tracking of Cooperation Framework indicators, milestones and results; follow-up on reporting commitments; and preparation of analytical products and evidence for Results Group, MEL Group and UNCT reviews. The incumbent will support the United Nations Country Team (UNCT), Results Groups and the Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Group through the consolidation, validation and quality assurance of agency inputs; tracking of Cooperation Framework indicators, milestones and results; follow-up on reporting commitments; and preparation of analytical products and evidence for Results Group, MEL Group and UNCT reviews and discussions. This position is located within the Office of the United Nations Resident Coordinator (Head RCO) in Nairobi, Kenya and reports to the Development Coordination Officer (Data Management and Results Monitoring/Reporting), under the overall guidance of the Head of RCO.
